teaser.text: Intel designs and manufactures the chips that make computers work, and it is trying to sell the manufacturing itself as a service. Its business is easiest to understand by following a dollar from a computer maker or cloud operator through design, factories, packaging and the costs that determine what Intel keeps.

blocks.heading: Where could Intel Corp.'s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast puts Intel below today’s $107.08 share price at every date. The weighted price is $85.88 in October 2027, a return of negative 20% including dividends. It reaches $89.04 in October 2028, a negative 17% return. It reaches $93.04 in October 2029, a negative 13% return. The October 2029 range is wide: $22.66 in the bear case to $195.64 in the bull case. The base case is most likely, but the outcome depends on whether Intel turns improved operations into self-funded factory economics.
The bear case carries a 32% probability. The base case carries 50%. The bull case carries 18%. The forecast range runs from $22.66 in the bear case to $195.64 in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Intel Corp.'s forecast?

paragraphs.text: The EBITDA proxy rises in the base case from $17,000 million in October 2027 to $20,000 million in October 2028 and $23,000 million in October 2029. The June quarter supports a recovery: revenue was $16,128 million and operating income was $1,796 million. Guidance points to gradual improvement, with quarterly revenue expected between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion. The bear case falls to $12,000 million, then $10,000 million, before recovering to $11,000 million because PC weakness, pricing pressure and poor utilization could overwhelm 18A progress. The bull case reaches $20,500 million, $27,000 million and $33,000 million as yields, server demand, packaging orders and 14A customer volume improve. Risk production is planned for late 2027 and high-volume production for 2028, so the forecast delays major 14A benefits.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Intel Corp. really make?

paragraphs.text: Intel generated US$9,697 million from operations and spent US$14,646 million on capital spending. The resulting free-cash-flow shortfall was US$4,949 million. Free cash flow is what remains after the business pays for the equipment and facilities needed to operate. The improvement from the previous year was substantial, but lower investment did most of the work.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Intel Corp. today?

paragraphs.text: At today’s $107.08, Intel’s market value is $540,112 million. A forward price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares the share price with expected profit. Intel’s 50.0x forward P/E means investors pay $50 for each $1 of profit expected over the next year. That implies about $2.14 of earnings per share. The price works only if that future profit arrives.

blocks.heading: Did Intel Corp.’s pay awards meet their targets?

paragraphs.text: His 2025 bonus was $2.374 million and used revenue, gross margin, operating expenses and operating milestones. Gross margin is what remains after the direct cost of supplying products. The 2023 PSU awards vested at 76% of target, showing that awards can fall short.

blocks.heading: How have Intel Corp.’s results changed over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Across the eight-quarter record available, Intel exceeded recorded revenue estimates every quarter. Adjusted earnings beat in five of those quarters, and the latest four all showed beats. That record is encouraging, but different services use different analyst samples.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Intel Corp.’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next evidence must show whether stronger sales are becoming cash and whether manufacturing milestones are becoming dependable supply.

Intel reports third-quarter results on October 29, 2026. Sales and earnings will test its guidance, but cash deserves equal attention. Free cash flow usually means operating cash left after capital expenditure. Intel’s adjusted measure also includes specified partner, incentive and lease flows.
